Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy
Re: Creative Group Facilitator, Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Team,
I recently came across your Creative Group Facilitator opening and wanted to introduce myself. I understand the position may have been filled, but I would welcome consideration for this or future opportunities with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

My background brings together adolescent behavioral health support, recovery group facilitation, visual arts education, and fitness and wellness programming. 

At Family Center for Recovery, I supported adolescents and adults in structured treatment settings. At Futures Recovery Healthcare, I facilitated recovery support groups and helped alumni connect with resources and coping strategies. More recently, as an art teacher, I have designed creative activities that encourage confidence, expression, and engagement.

I am especially drawn to opportunities to help young people strengthen self-esteem and positive self-talk through art, movement, drama-inspired expression, and mindfulness. My approach values practical DBT-informed skills and creative activities as complements to the work of licensed treatment professionals.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my experience might support your programming. I have attached my resume for your consideration. 

Thank you for your time.

Warm regards, Jennifer Winston

candidates.cover_letter:
Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Committee,

I am applying for the Clinical Director position with your private mental health practice. As a
Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor, National Certified Counselor, and private practice
co-owner and program director, I bring more than 15 years of mental health experience and a
strong understanding of the connection between quality clinical care, clinician support, and
effective practice operations. I am drawn to this opportunity because I want to help shape a
practice where clients receive thoughtful, consistent care and clinicians have the guidance and
support to do their best work.

In my role with Life & Wellness Counseling and Consulting, PLLC, I provide clinical supervision to
contract therapists, train administrative staff on ethics and HIPAA-compliant policies and
procedures, conduct internal clinical record audits, and prepare documentation for insurance
review. Maintaining an outpatient caseload alongside these responsibilities keeps me connected
to the realities of clinical work and the importance of clear expectations, sound documentation,
and practical support for staff.

My work as Therapist III at Novant Health Psychiatry-Southpark includes comprehensive clinical
assessments, diagnosis and level-of-care recommendations, individualized treatment planning,
individual and family therapy, and collaboration with physicians and other providers. My
previous experience at Safe Alliance strengthened my work with survivors of sexual assault and
domestic violence, while intensive in-home team leadership and community-based roles
developed my skills in staff supervision, crisis planning, and coordination across systems.

As Clinical Director, I would bring a collaborative leadership approach grounded in ethical
practice, accountability, and respect for both clients and staff. I would welcome the opportunity
to strengthen clinical processes, support professional development, and contribute to a practice
culture that values quality, consistency, and compassionate care. My experience balancing
clinical and administrative responsibilities has prepared me to contribute to these priorities.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my
clinical experience and leadership background align with your practice's needs and goals.

Kind regards,

Allegra Cooper, MA, LCMHC

Licensed Clinical Mental Health Counselor and National Certified Counselor with more than 15
years of experience across outpatient, intensive in-home, community, and institutional mental
health settings. Combines direct clinical care with experience as a private practice co-owner and
program director, including clinical supervision, staff training, documentation review, and
preparation for insurance audits. Brings a person-centered approach to supporting clients,
developing clinicians, and maintaining consistent standards of care.

Clinical Leadership & Practice Operations

As Co-Owner, Program Director, and Outpatient Therapist at Life & Wellness Counseling and
Consulting, PLLC, provides clinical supervision to contract therapists and trains administrative
staff on ethics and HIPAA-compliant policies and procedures. Conducts internal clinical record
audits and prepares documentation for insurance review while maintaining an outpatient
caseload. Also contributes to practice visibility through presentations, marketing events, and

Assessment, Treatment & Care Coordination

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Program Coordinator position. What drew me to this opportunity is the chance to support adolescents and their families during a time when having consistent, compassionate, and accessible mental health care can make such a meaningful difference.

Throughout my experience in behavioral health, I have found that the work I value most involves supporting children and families while contributing to the teams responsible for their care. As an RBT and Student Analyst, I have worked closely with children and families, assisted with initial assessments and reassessments, contributed to treatment planning, supported parent training, and collaborated with multidisciplinary providers. These experiences have given me a strong understanding of the importance of communication, documentation, and teamwork in behavioral health services.

In addition to my clinical experience, my previous role as a Health Assistant gave me a strong foundation in healthcare administration and remote client support. I worked with clients to verify insurance benefits, reviewed coverage information, assisted with claims and payment-related inquiries, and handled a high volume of calls while communicating with English- and Spanish-speaking families. This experience strengthened my ability to multitask, navigate administrative processes, maintain accurate information, and provide helpful, professional support in a remote setting.

My experience as a Child Protective Investigator also shaped the way I approach family communication. It taught me the importance of listening without judgment, handling sensitive situations with care, and recognizing when concerns need to be communicated or escalated. I believe these skills would be especially valuable when supporting adolescents and families participating in AWA's virtual program.

As a bilingual English and Spanish speaker, I would love the opportunity to help families feel comfortable navigating the admissions process, staying connected with the program, and understanding important updates. I am particularly interested in bringing together my behavioral health and administrative experience in a role that allows me to contribute to the day-to-day operations of a program making a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, experience, and genuine interest in supporting young people could contribute to the AWA team.

Warmly,
Josmari Arroyo

My name is Corey Ann, and I’m the founder of Gypsy Jasmine Wellness. I’m a wellness practitioner with a background in yoga, personal training, mindful movement, and holistic wellness. My approach integrates movement, breathwork, somatic practices, fascia release, and mindfulness to support the mind-body connection and promote overall well-being.

My own journey with chronic pain and recovery has shaped my passion for this work and strengthened my belief in the importance of compassionate, individualized wellness support. I strive to create spaces where people feel supported, empowered, and encouraged to explore their own path toward greater well being.

I would welcome the opportunity to connect, learn more about your organization, and explore how my experience and offerings might complement your existing programs.

October 28, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in youth development, art instruction, creative education, and community programming, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an environment dedicated to supporting adolescents’ well-being, personal development, and growth.

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

In Community,

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) and Principles Recovery Center (PRC). With a degree in Sociology and an extensive background spanning case management, law enforcement, and youth corrections, I have dedicated my career to supporting individuals and families during some of the hardest moments of their lives. I am eager to bring my calm, compassionate presence and system-navigation expertise to your admissions team.

Throughout my career in case management and youth corrections, I have worked directly with teens, adults, and families facing acute mental health and substance use challenges. My background in law enforcement trained me to remain grounded, empathetic, and clear-headed during high-stress situations, while my case management experience taught me how to listen without judgment and guide clients toward practical next steps. Whether I am speaking with an overwhelmed parent seeking help for their teenager or an adult ready to address substance use, I excel at explaining complex care options—such as Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP) and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP)—in plain, reassuring language.

In addition to crisis de-escalation and client advocacy, I bring strong operational and administrative skills essential for a remote admissions role:
•	Client Assessment and Care Navigation: Experienced in conducting thorough initial screenings, evaluating client needs, and connecting individuals with appropriate mental health, substance use, and community resources.
•	Coordination and Follow-Through: Proven ability to coordinate multi-agency assessments, manage intake documentation, verify benefits, and maintain consistent, compassionate follow-up until every individual is scheduled or referred to the right care.
•	Confidentiality and Documentation: Accustomed to working under strict confidentiality and HIPAA compliance standards, ensuring every interaction and lead is accurately tracked across case management, CRM, and EMR systems.
•	
I deeply admire the dual mission of AWA and PRC to provide specialized, accessible care for both adolescents and adults. My Sociology background gives me a strong understanding of the family dynamics and systemic barriers clients often face when reaching out for help, allowing me to meet every caller with genuine empathy and actionable support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background in case management, youth services, and crisis support can help your team guide more individuals and families toward recovery.

Sincerely,
Garrett Sheil

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring both my professional experience and personal perspective to your team. I am passionate about helping young people find the support they need and would love to contribute to a program that can make a lasting difference in their lives.

Thank you for your time and consideration, I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,
Emma Kasti

Vanessa McFarlen
Cambridge, Minnesota
November 10, 2026

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Remote Intake Advisor position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I have experience working in a call center, customer service, and childcare, which has helped me develop strong communication skills, patience, and the ability to connect with people from different backgrounds.

Mental health is something that means a lot to me personally. I lost my father to suicide and have watched people close to me struggle with mental health and substance abuse. I have also seen how much strength it takes to work toward recovery. These experiences have given me a strong desire to help others who may be going through some of the hardest times in their lives.

I know that asking for help isn’t always easy, and I want to be someone who makes that first step a little less scary. I believe everyone deserves to feel heard, understood, and supported without judgment.

I am hardworking, dependable, compassionate, and always willing to learn. Although I haven’t worked directly in the mental health field, I believe my personal experiences and professional skills would allow me to make a positive difference.

Thank you for considering my application. I would love the opportunity to be part of a team that helps individuals and families find the support they need.

Sincerely,
Vanessa McFarlen

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a professional background in behavioral health, care coordination, substance use counseling, and healthcare administration, I am confident in my ability to provide compassionate, organized, and effective support to individuals and families seeking treatment.

In my current role as a Care Coordinator and Substance Use Counselor at Intermountain Centers, I work closely with adolescents, families, healthcare providers, and community agencies to coordinate behavioral health services and ensure individuals receive appropriate levels of care. My responsibilities include conducting assessments, coordinating referrals, facilitating Child and Family Team (CFT) meetings, assisting families with treatment planning, and supporting individuals through complex behavioral health challenges. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate with individuals in distress, identify service needs, and guide families through the treatment process with empathy and professionalism.

I also bring experience working within Arizona’s behavioral health system, including coordinating services with Medicaid-funded programs, maintaining accurate clinical documentation, and collaborating with multidisciplinary treatment teams. I understand the importance of timely follow-up, confidentiality, HIPAA compliance, and clear communication when helping individuals access mental health and substance use treatment.

As a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking professional, I am able to support diverse populations and help reduce language barriers that may prevent individuals and families from accessing care. I hold a Master of Business Administration (MBA) and a Master of Healthcare Administration (MHA), and I am currently completing my Master’s degree in Addiction Psychology at Arizona State University. This combination of clinical knowledge and administrative education allows me to approach admissions coordination with both compassion and operational efficiency.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to serve as a supportive first point of contact for adolescents, adults, and families during challenging moments. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be overwhelming, and I believe every individual deserves to be met with patience, dignity, and reassurance.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, dedication, and commitment to accessible behavioral healthcare to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications align with the needs of your programs.

Sincerely, 
Leslie Bright

Strong ability to build rapport with families, assess needs, communicate effectively, and guide families through the process of accessing services and treatment.

work_history.title: Program Manager
work_history.summary: Experienced in leading and coordinating teams supporting children, youth, and families in community-based programs. Develop and maintain strong working relationships with families, school personnel, community partners, and service providers. Coordinate staff schedules, program activities, transportation, and service needs to ensure effective program operations. Monitor staff performance, program quality, documentation, attendance, and compliance with organizational policies and procedures. Provide leadership, guidance, coaching, and support to staff while promoting a positive and collaborative team environment. Support the safety, well-being, and positive development of children through appropriate supervision, positive guidance, and crisis intervention. Maintain accurate records, case documentation, incident reports, and other required program documentation. Communicate effectively with parents, staff, school personnel, community agencies, and management. Assist with program planning, resource coordination, supplies, and day-to-day administrative responsibilities. Experienced working with children and families from diverse backgrounds and connecting families with community resources and services. Strong organizational, communication, problem-solving, and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple responsibilities in a fast-paced environment.

work_history.title: Youth Screening Specialist
work_history.summary: Conducts interviews and follows detention screening criteria, for all youth taken into custody, to determine eligibility for release, respite care, supervised release, or secure detention. Conducts youth interviews to make appropriate State Attorney recommendations for all youth screened. Ensures each youth receives medical and mental health clearance prior to admission to the JAC (juvenile assessment center), or screening processing area. Reviews law enforcement paperwork and criminal history records. Acts as a resource for families, outside agencies and staff answers telephones. Maintains accurate records, to include youth files, screening packets, and documentation in the Departments Juvenile Justice Information System (JJIS). Communicates with youth's parents/guardians, Department of Juvenile Justice and/or Department of Children and Families staff, and law enforcement to ensure efficient and accurate processing of youth. Attend court hearings as needed to present findings of detention risk assessment. Provides crisis intervention to de-escalate immediate conflict situations as needed. Provides sight and sound supervision of youth at risk for self-harm. Completes installations of EM (electronic monitoring) equipment on youth based on assessment score or court order. Assesses suicide risk and complete mental health and substance abuse screenings. Utilizes Motivational Interviewing and Trauma-Informed Care techniques to effectively conduct all interviews and assessment requirements during the screening process. Performs other related duties as assigned.

work_history.title: Health Educator
work_history.summary: Establish and maintain trust, serve as a liaison between health/social services and Healthy Start participants in the community. Facilitate access to services and work to provide high quality and culturally competent service delivery in their scope. Supports participant and community capacity, using their experience and knowledge. Increase perinatal health knowledge and self-sufficiency through activities like outreach, community education, informal counseling, social support, and advocacy. Explain what preconception/after conception care is, why it is important, and discuss its basic components. Identify warning signs and symptoms that mother and/or baby may be at risk and act if necessary to connect participants to appropriate services. Assist participants in developing and carrying out a reproductive life plan, identifying medical and social risk factors that might put a future pregnancy at risk. Help identify goals, barriers to change, and support for change, including personal strengths and problem-solving abilities. Understand organizational policies and procedures and ensure screening and assessment is conducted consistently with these policies and procedures. Use Healthy Start forms and/or data collection and assessment tools, to better understand participants, their families, and their communities.

work_history.summary: Leads, guides, and directs a team of Family Support workers, creates, and coordinates weekly schedules for children and a staff schedule for overnight care for children without placement. Actively engage with youth and provide all necessary support to meet their needs, including all direct care and service requirements. Follows active treatment/programming. Creates and sends out weekly emails for weekly/weekend day service requests for children in the office. Plans performance expectations and monitors efficiency of work. Participate in staffing, court hearing and other team meetings related to the provision of services to children and families. Coordinate necessary transportation for families. Assist in supervising children in absence of parents or those awaiting placement. Monitor quality of care by contacting families by phone and supervising court ordered supervised visits. Develop and maintain effective work relationships with case managers, families and community resource services including medical professionals, law enforcement, therapist, school officials, utilizing referral resources, as necessary. Cleveland Clinic Indian River Hospital- Healthy Start Coalition

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Wellness Academy Hiring Team,
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Wellness Academy. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology and a minor in Human Development and Family Studies, I have developed a strong passion for understanding child and adolescent development, mental health, and the importance of providing individuals and families with the support and resources they need.
My interest in mental health has been both academic and personal. Growing up, I witnessed close friends experience mental health challenges and saw firsthand how deeply these struggles can affect an individual's well-being, relationships, and everyday life. These experiences inspired me to pursue psychology and strengthened my belief in the importance of early intervention, accessible mental health resources, and compassionate support.
Through my academic studies, I gained a deeper understanding of human behavior, developmental stages, and the factors that influence emotional and mental well-being. My minor in Human Development and Family Studies also expanded my understanding of family dynamics, cultural and economic differences, childhood experiences, and different environments that shape an individual's development.
In addition to my education, my customer service experience, both in person and over the phone, has helped me develop strong communication, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills. I have learned how to actively listen, adapt to different personalities, navigate difficult conversations, and deescalate challenging situations while remaining patient and professional. These experiences have taught me the importance of making people feel heard, respected, and understood, which I believe is especially important when working with families seeking mental health services.
I am particularly drawn to this position because I recognize that the admissions process is often a family's first interaction with a mental health organization. I would love the opportunity to help make that experience welcoming and reassuring by communicating with empathy, providing support, and helping families feel comfortable taking the next step toward receiving care.
I would bring a genuine passion for mental health, strong communication skills, attention to detail, and a willingness to learn and grow within the organization. I am excited about the opportunity to combine my educational background and customer service experience to make a meaningful difference in the lives of children and families.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward for the opportunity to talk with you further. 
Sincerely, 
Charisse N Blyden

candidates.cover_letter:
Kayla Gillin
Riverview, Florida
813-614-2352

November 9, 2026

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I have several years of healthcare experience, including working directly with children and adolescents experiencing mental health challenges. I will also be graduating from St. Petersburg College on December 14, 2026, with my Bachelor’s degree in Human Services. I believe my education, professional experience, and passion for helping others would make me a great addition to your team.

In my previous role as a Mental Health Patient Care Technician at St. Joseph’s Children’s Hospital, I worked closely with children and adolescents experiencing mental health crises, behavioral challenges, and various psychiatric disorders. Many of the patients I encountered had complex backgrounds, including experiences in group homes, difficult family situations, and underlying mental health conditions. Through this experience, I developed a deeper understanding of how important it is to connect with these individuals beyond their diagnosis or current circumstances. I made it a priority to build rapport with my patients, understand their behaviors, and create an environment where they felt comfortable, respected, and supported.

One of the things I am particularly proud of is creating a pediatric behavioral health report sheet to improve communication between staff members during patient handoffs. I recognized that caring for behavioral health patients should involve more than simply observing them throughout a 12 hour shift. My goal was to help staff better understand each patient’s background, behaviors, emotional needs, potential triggers, and any history of self harming behaviors or statements. Having this information readily available helped support more meaningful patient interactions, improved continuity of care, and provided valuable observations that could be communicated to psychiatrists, behavioral health therapists, and other members of the treatment team.

Working with these patients gave me a genuine appreciation for the challenges children and adolescents face when dealing with mental health conditions. I learned that building trust, listening without judgment, and taking the time to understand someone’s experiences can make a significant difference in how they respond to care. This experience strengthened my communication skills, patience, compassion, and ability to work with individuals during some of their most vulnerable moments.

In addition to my behavioral health experience, my previous role as a NICU Nurse Technician at Tampa General Hospital strengthened my ability to remain organized, communicate effectively with families, maintain accurate documentation, and work collaboratively with healthcare professionals. My education in Human Services and my 180 hour internship have also expanded my knowledge of mental health, community resources, and connecting individuals and families with appropriate services.

I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an emotional and overwhelming experience for both adolescents and their families. I would love the opportunity to use my background to help families feel comfortable, informed, and supported throughout the admissions process. I believe my ability to connect with people, understand their concerns, and approach difficult situations with empathy would allow me to make a positive impact in this position.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to further discuss how my experience, education, and dedication to supporting children and families align with the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Kayla Gillin

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Mooresville, NC

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker Associate (LCSWA) with a Master of Social Work degree and three years of experience supporting children, adolescents, and families, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to AWA's mission of providing compassionate, evidence-based mental health services to adolescents. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to join the founding clinical team and help establish a supportive, collaborative, and client-centered therapeutic environment.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong foundation in family-centered treatment, crisis intervention, case management, treatment planning, and trauma-informed care. In my current role as a Family Centered Treatment Specialist with Pinnacle Family Services, I provide individualized treatment and case management services to children and families in home and community settings. I develop treatment plans, facilitate interventions, collaborate with community partners, and support families in navigating challenges while promoting stability, resilience, and improved outcomes. This experience has strengthened my ability to build therapeutic relationships, identify individual and family needs, and implement interventions that support meaningful behavioral and emotional change.

Previously, as a Family Advocate at Pat's Place Child Advocacy Center, I supported children and families navigating difficult and often traumatic circumstances. I provided emotional support, crisis intervention, resource coordination, and advocacy while collaborating with multidisciplinary professionals to prioritize child safety and family well-being. My school social work experience at Hawthorne Academy further strengthened my ability to recognize and address the emotional, behavioral, academic, and social needs of at-risk students while developing interventions and connecting families with appropriate resources.

I believe my background in child and family services provides a valuable foundation for working with adolescents experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, behavioral challenges, and other mental health concerns. I am passionate about creating a therapeutic space where adolescents feel safe, understood, and empowered to develop healthy coping strategies and recognize their strengths. I also understand the importance of family involvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, individualized treatment planning, and consistent communication in supporting successful clinical outcomes.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, dedication to family-centered care, and passion for adolescent mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Being part of a new program would allow me to contribute not only to the care of adolescents and their families but also to the development of a positive clinical culture built on compassion, collaboration, and excellence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, experience, and commitment to serving children and families would make me a valuable addition to AWA's founding clinical team.

Sincerely,

Abigail Cornele, MSW, LCSWA

To whom it may concern,
My name is Selena, and I am excited to be applying for the primary therapist position at North Carolina's first-ever AWA location! I am an LCSWA with multiple years of experience providing therapeutic support in numerous capacities, including as a behavioral health technician, case manager, and psychotherapist. I've also gained experience in a diverse range of therapeutic settings, such as an inpatient adolescent hospital, PHP/IOP mental health clinics, community health (including in-home), and outpatient therapy. The most influential experiences I've gained have been working in adolescent inpatient and PHP/IOP clinics, in which I became comfortable leading group therapy sessions, providing 1:1 individual therapy as well as family-based therapy, and working collaboratively with clinical teams consisting of numerous disciplines and treatment goals. I've also become comfortable with higher levels of care, which I am able to use to offer clients validation and unconditional positive regard, as these experiences can be exhausting. In my current outpatient work, I primarily work with pre-teens and adolescents, as I witnessed a gap in care for these age groups despite the intensity of these transformative years. I aspire to be a supportive resource to these clients in whatever capacity I am able to, as it is already difficult to be a teen, let alone one who feels misunderstood and alone in the journey.
